q: Plants make their own ___ molecules, using the process of photosynthesis. (2025- Set 7)
e: Plants synthesize organic molecules through photosynthesis using carbon dioxide, water, and sunlight.

q: Plants make their own organic molecules, using the process of ___. (2025- Set 9)
e: Photosynthesis is the metabolic process by which plants produce organic molecules.

q: The main photosynthetic organs are the ___. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အများစုတွင်မေး) (2025-Set 12)
e: Leaves are the primary photosynthetic organs in most plants.

q: Glucose can be moved through the ___ as part of the sucrose molecule. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Phloem tissue transports sucrose synthesized from glucose throughout the plant.

q: Xylem, which transports water and ___ ions from the roots to all parts of the plant. (2026- Set 2)
e: Xylem carries water along with dissolved inorganic mineral ions from the soil.

q: In a plant, the dissolved organic compounds are transported in the ___ tissue. (2025- Set 5)
e: Phloem tissue is responsible for translocating dissolved organic nutrients.

q: The uptake of ___ can be passive transport such as diffusion and osmosis. (2025- Set 1)
e: Mineral uptake by root cells can occur passively via diffusion along concentration gradients.

q: In plant, the dissolved mineral ions are transported in the ___ tissue. (2024-Set 3)
e: Xylem transports water and dissolved mineral ions upward from roots.

q: The dissolved mineral ions are transported in the ___ tissue. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Dissolved mineral ions are carried through the xylem tissue.

q: The dissolved mineral ions are transported in the ___. (2025-Set 4)
e: Xylem tissue serves as the primary conduit for mineral ions.

q: In passive absorption, water moves through the ___ of the root. (2025- Set 6)
e: The apoplast pathway allows water to move through non-living cell walls during passive absorption.

q: In hot conditions, transpiration plays an important role in cooling the ___. (2026- Set 1)
e: Evaporative cooling caused by transpiration prevents leaves from overheating.

q: Stomata must be opened during the day to allow carbon dioxide to diffuse into the leaf for ___. (2026- နိုင်ငံခြား) (2025- Set 11)
e: Carbon dioxide intake through open stomata is essential for photosynthesis.

q: Stomata must be opened during the day to allow ___ to diffuse into the leaf for photosynthesis. (2025- Set 7)
e: Carbon dioxide diffuses into leaves via stomatal openings during daylight.

q: Most transpiration takes place through the ___. (2024-Set 2 / 2025-Set 8)
e: The majority of water loss during transpiration occurs through stomata.

q: In hot conditions, ___ plays an important role in cooling the leaves. (2024-Set 4)
e: Transpiration provides cooling to plant leaves through water evaporation.

q: Carbohydrates are transported out of the leaf in the form of ___ to the stem. (2025- Set 10)
e: Carbohydrates are converted to sucrose for translocational transport through phloem.

q: Water and dissolved salts from the soil travel upwards through the ___ of the xylem. (2025- Set 13)
e: Xylem vessels form continuous hollow tubes that transport water and salts upward.

q: Within any organisms, ___ need to be moved from one place to anothr. (2026-Set 1) (2025-Set2,5)
e: Internal transport systems carry various essential substances across organismal tissues.

q: Birds and mammals need much more ___ than fish. (2025- Set 9)
e: Endothermic birds and mammals require large quantities of oxygen to support high metabolic rates.

q: The right ventricle pumps blood to the ___, which are relatively close to the heart. (2025- Set 1)
e: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to nearby lungs for oxygenation.

q: The function of ___ valve is prevention of back-flow of blood from the right ventricle into right atrium. (2026- နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: The tricuspid valve closes to prevent blood backflow into the right atrium.

q: The function of the ___ is prevention of backflow of blood from the right ventricle into the right atrium. (2025- Set 11)
e: The tricuspid valve maintains unidirectional blood flow from right atrium to right ventricle.

q: The human heart is a muscular pump with ___ chambers. (2024-Set 3)
e: The human heart comprises four distinct chambers: two atria and two ventricles.

q: The pulmonary artery carrying deoxygenated blood from the ___ to the lungs. (2025- Set 6)
e: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.

q: The very smallest branches of the arterial system are ___. (2024-Set 2)
e: Arterioles represent the smallest arterial branches leading to capillary networks.

q: The very smallest branches of the arterial system, furthest from the heart, are the ___. (2025-Set 4)
e: Arterioles are fine arterial vessels regulating blood flow into capillaries.

q: ___ carry blood away from the heart towards the cells of the body. (2024-Set 4)
e: Arteries are blood vessels that transport blood away from the heart.

q: Veins carry blood back towards the ___. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား : 2025-Set 3)
e: Veins function to transport blood from tissue capillary beds back toward the heart.

q: Platelets are ___ fragments of large cells called megakaryocytes. (2026-Set 2)
e: Platelets are tiny cell fragments formed by megakaryocytes.

q: Platelets are tiny fragments of large cells called ___. (2025- Set 13)
e: Megakaryocytes are giant bone marrow cells that fragment into blood platelets.

q: The ___ transport oxygen from the lungs to all the cells. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အများစုတွင်မေး : 2025-Set 8)
e: Erythrocytes contain hemoglobin to transport oxygen from lungs to tissues.

q: Which of the following vitamin is necessary for blood clotting? ___ (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Vitamin K is essential for synthesizing prothrombin and other clotting factors.

q: Lymph nodes contain ___. (2025- Set 12)
e: Lymph nodes are packed with white blood cells that trap pathogens and fight infection.
